payload.name: waveform-coding
payload.scope: So a continuous signal can be carried and stored at a fixed reduced bit rate with its waveform shape preserved, in contrast to parametric coding, which transmits only a model of the source.

definition.body: Waveform-coding is a human-made family of signal-coding procedures that encode the signal's own waveform - the sequence of sample amplitudes - rather than a model of the source, so a continuous signal can be carried or stored at a fixed reduced bit rate with the waveform shape preserved. The family's procedures act on the waveform itself: pulse-code modulation quantizes the sample values directly; delta modulation encodes the difference between successive samples; adaptive differential pulse-code modulation quantizes the prediction error against an adaptive predictor; sigma-delta modulation emits an oversampled one-bit feedback stream. Parameters that define the class: (1) the bit commitment to the waveform, fixed or adaptive; (2) the representation of each sample - direct amplitude level, successive difference, or prediction error; (3) the reconstruction rule that maps the code word back to a sample. Persistence mechanism: specified in the ITU-T G.711, G.721, G.726 standards and the CD Red Book, described in the speech-coding literature as the waveform-coding class alongside parametric and hybrid coding, and implemented in telephony, music disc, and audio-coding practice. e.g.: the G.711 mu-law PCM codec in a T1 voice path; the G.726 24 kbit/s ADPCM codec in an ISDN voice channel; the 16-bit linear PCM of a Red Book CD track | not: linear predictive coding which transmits a model of the vocal tract rather than the waveform; the code-excited linear prediction of G.729 which synthesizes speech from codebook excitation through a synthesis filter; transform coding of a coefficient vector in the frequency domain [formal: codificatio formae undae | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes]

payload.scope: So that a continuous signal can be carried at one bit per sample, below the rate where a multi-bit quantizer is worth its complexity, with a one-sample prediction stage preserving most of the waveform.

definition.body: Delta modulation is a human-made one-bit predictive waveform-coding procedure that transmits, for each new sample, only the sign of the difference between the sample and the previously reconstructed value, so a continuous signal can be carried on one bit per sample. Procedure: (1) a predictor holds the last reconstructed sample; (2) the encoder compares the new sample with it and transmits one bit, up or down; (3) the decoder reconstructs the sample as the previous sample plus or minus a step, fixed in basic delta modulation and adapted to the signal slope in adaptive delta modulation. Parameters: (1) the bit commitment, one bit per sample; (2) the step size, fixed or adaptive; (3) the predictor order, the previous sample in first-order delta modulation, a linear combination in differential forms; (4) the sampling rate, at the Nyquist rate in classic delta modulation, where oversampled one-bit variants with noise-shaped feedback are sigma-delta modulation instead. Persistence mechanism: proposed by Zeller in 1948 for long-distance telephone lines, realized in Bell System first-order delta-modulation voice experiments at 256 kbit/s, carried in the differential lineage of the ITU-T G.721 and G.726 standards, and described in the coding literature as the one-bit ancestor of differential pulse-code modulation. e.g.: Zeller's 1948 delta modulation proposal for long-distance telephone lines; first-order delta modulation voice channel at 256 kbit/s in Bell System experiments; one-bit delta modulation telemetry channel in a satellite downlink | not: sigma-delta modulation (oversampled one-bit noise-shaped feedback stream); pulse-code modulation (multi-bit quantizer on the full sample, no prediction stage); adaptive differential pulse-code modulation (multi-bit prediction-error quantizer, G.726) [formal: modulatio deltae | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes]
